Hi Emilia — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, then a quick explanation and attachments.

1) EU POC processing: By default for EU customers we deploy and run inference in EU regions (primary: eu-west-1 / eu-west-3 depending on availability). Customer request payloads, KV cache, and persistent logs for the POC will remain in the selected EU region.

2) Subprocessors (EU footprint): compute (AWS EMEA: eu-west-1 / eu-west-3), object storage (GCP europe-west3 or AWS S3 in EU), CDN/edge (Fastly in EU POPs), metrics (Datadog EU region), secrets/KMS (HashiCorp Vault / customer KMS integrations), and telemetry pipelines (Sumo Logic or self-hosted collectors). Detailed matrix attached.

3) Retention defaults: request logs (30 days), KV cache (ephemeral by default; caches live until TTL expiry — default 24 hours for inference sessions), telemetry/metrics (90 days). These are configurable: for a POC we can reduce request logs to 7 days and set cache TTLs to your preference. We can also opt you into a private deployment (VPC) or Dedicated pool if you need isolation.

I've attached a short residency & subprocessor matrix (redwood-residency-subprocessor-matrix-2026.pdf) and a SOC2 snapshot. Laura is on this thread for any deeper security controls or legal asks.

Next steps I suggest: 1) Laura/Prioyam to confirm KMS options and SCC/DPA language, 2) we share the matrix with your security team, 3) schedule a follow-up for detailed network diagrams if needed.

Hi Emilia — adding Laura (Security) and Priyom (Infra) to provide the technical confirmations you asked for. Summary answers below + proposed next steps.

1) Deletion workflow and SLA
- Immediate actions: when Arx requests full deletion we trigger a coordinated wipe across the control plane and the EU data plane. This includes: primary object storage objects, request logs, and persistent artifacts.
- Cache/KV: in-memory and on-disk KV caches are invalidated immediately; background compaction may remove persisted shards within 1–6 hours depending on shard state.
- Audit trail: we retain a minimal audit record showing that deletion was executed (timestamp + operator id) for compliance; content is irreversibly deleted.
- SLA: standard POC deletion SLA is 72 hours for full verification; for Enterprise contracts we can negotiate 24-hour verified deletion.

2) KMS / Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK)
- Supported providers: AWS KMS (customer-managed CMKs), Google Cloud KMS, Azure Key Vault, and HSM integrations (via Vault).
- Modes: you can configure customer-managed keys for object encryption and for encrypting persisted cache snapshots. Keys can be rotated and we support key wrapping so Redwood never has plaintext access.

3) Cross-border fallback and routing controls
- Default behavior: for EU-pinned customers we do not route inference requests outside the chosen EU data plane for normal operations.
- Fallbacks: automatic cross-border fallback only occurs under severe region-wide capacity failures or declared disaster conditions and only to pre-approved fallback regions (we will not do ad-hoc routing to the US without explicit customer approval).
- Control: we can provide a hard pin in your tenant configuration that disallows any cross-border routing; this is the recommended setting for regulated EU customers.

Subprocessor clarifications: compute (AWS eu-west-1 / AWS eu-west-3), storage (GCP europe-west3 or S3 eu), edge (Fastly EU), metrics (Datadog EU), logs pipeline (Sumo Logic or self-hosted), secrets (HashiCorp Vault), monitoring/alerting (PagerDuty). We will provide the complete subprocessor contract list and SCC/DPA language as part of the onboarding pack.

- If you want a BYOK setup for the POC we can provision a Dedicated pool with customer KMS; Laura can follow up with the exact integration steps.
